solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

indicators.note: to flip something over is to turn it the other way, so the joined letters run backwards

parts.note: brut describes very dry champagne or sparkling wine

explanation.surface: Instructions for drying a fish: turn it over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flip over' turns TOBRUT (TO beside BRUT) end to end.
explanation.definitionFit: A turbot is a large flatfish prized for the table.

clue.text: One translated secret code for free

parts.note: un is French for one, so the word one put into French
a PIN is the personal number you keep secret for a bank card

explanation.surface: Someone translated a secret code to set something loose.
explanation.definitionFit: To unpin is to unfasten, freeing what was held down; both are verbs.

parts.note: brassy means cheeky or brazen; its comparative means more insolent

explanation.surface: An English backer who is cheekier than the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporter' suggests a fan; it is underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A bra is a garment that supports the bust, so it is jocularly a supporter.

clue.text: Sticky on the road? Drag one's feet

definitions.meaning: covered in tar, the black gummy stuff used to surface roads
to linger or delay instead of getting on

explanation.surface: A sticky road surface slows you down.
explanation.definitionFit: Tar-coated surfaces are sticky, and to linger is to dawdle; the word is both adjective and verb.

clue.text: Juice knocked back, have a go at cake

indicators.note: knocking something back sends it the other way, so the word for juice is read in reverse

parts.note: sap is the juice of a plant
to try is to have a go

explanation.surface: Someone downs a drink and then tries some cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' reads like drinking; here it reverses SAP into PAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastry is a single small sweet baked item, a kind of cake.

parts.note: a part is a bit or portion
a ridge is a raised edge or crest

explanation.surface: A bird that is slightly nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on edge' looks like a single phrase for nervous; 'on' only places RIDGE after PART.
explanation.definitionFit: The partridge is a plump game bird of fields and hedgerows.

definitions.meaning: workers or employees, as in farm hands

explanation.surface: A command or description: hands holding a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: Employees are collectively the workforce, and a pole or rod carried for walking has the same name.

clue.text: Liquid in garage boxes for all to see, one can measure water

indicators.note: to box something is to enclose it, so the rearranged letters go round the film rating
liquid means fluid, not fixed, so the letters of in and garage flow into a new order

parts.note: U is the British film certificate for universal viewing, suitable for everyone

explanation.surface: Liquid found in a garage, packed in boxes on show, can be gauged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liquid' looks like water, but it signals an anagram of IN GARAGE, giving RAINGAGE; 'boxes' puts U inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: This instrument collects and measures rainfall, so it is a device for measuring water.

parts.note: a can is a container that beer, for example, may come in
did means performed or carried out

explanation.surface: An opened beer was taken outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open' looks like opening the beer; it is the definition, meaning frank.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone open is frank and honest, holding nothing back.

indicators.note: to trouser is to pocket or take in, so the word for old holds the other piece

parts.note: aged means old
re means on or about, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: Asked if the old trousers are on, someone shouts yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trousers' looks like a garment but is a verb: AGED takes in RE.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of assent: saying you concur is saying yes.

clue.text: European character in a pub in part of California?

indicators.note: in places the pub abbreviation within the city letters

parts.note: LA, Los Angeles, is a city in California
PH is the map abbreviation for public house

explanation.surface: A European figure drinking in a bar somewhere in California.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European character' is a letter of the Greek alphabet, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: The first letter of the Greek alphabet, Greece being in Europe.

clue.text: Grenadier shot, looking at things again

indicators.note: something shot is wrecked or ruined, so the soldier's letters are scattered

explanation.surface: A soldier who was shot is going over things a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: Going through a text a second time means perusing it again.

clue.text: One in seven ignores a mean rule

indicators.note: to ignore something is to leave it out, so the A goes from the word

parts.note: a week holds seven days, so a day is one in seven
nasty means mean or unkind

explanation.surface: One person in seven disregards a cruel regulation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignores' drops the A from DAY, leaving DY.
explanation.definitionFit: A succession of rulers from one family; the line's reign can stand for its rule.

clue.text: Neanderthal comment by judge on Europeans, one seeking shelter

parts.note: a referee judges a game, shortened to ref
ug is the grunt cartoon cavemen are given
E for European, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A judge makes a caveman remark about Europeans who want sanctuary.
explanation.definitionFit: A displaced person fleeing danger looks for asylum or protection.

clue.text: Everton players initially entering in kit say, blue

indicators.note: the two initials go into the word for clothed

parts.note: dressed means clothed, wearing kit, for example

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letters of the two words before it

explanation.surface: Everton players turn out in kit and are glum, perhaps in their blue strip.
explanation.walkthrough: Everton is an English football club that plays in blue, so 'blue' feels like kit; it means sad.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling blue is feeling low or melancholy.

definitions.meaning: smeared thickly over a surface, as with plaster

explanation.surface: Two kitchen words: preserved in vinegar, and smeared on bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Drunk is one slang sense; smeared or daubed thickly is the other.

clue.text: Met tides, as if at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are in a muddle

explanation.surface: The tides met out at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A need or condition that has been met is fulfilled.

definitions.meaning: sure, as in sure to happen

explanation.surface: A sure dividing line.
explanation.definitionFit: Sure to happen is one sense; a limit or boundary line is the other.

parts.note: bottom means last, as at the foot of a league table
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: A final drink at closing time: down the hatch.
explanation.definitionFit: A drinking toast urging everyone to drain the glass.

indicators.note: first puts the alphabet letter at the front

parts.note: B is the second letter of the alphabet
a race is a people or nation

explanation.surface: Two people, one of whom comes second and goes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair, as in a couple of game birds shot together.

clue.text: Down-and-out finds something to eat in drinking establishment

indicators.note: in puts the food inside the drinking place

parts.note: a bar is a place for drinking
an egg is something to eat

explanation.surface: A vagrant gets a snack in a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A pauper who lives on alms; destitute people are down-and-outs.

indicators.note: rewritten says the letters are set down again in a different order

explanation.surface: A numbering word redrafted alongside a principle.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinal numbers give position in a sequence, like first or tenth.

indicators.note: wobbly means unsteady, so the letters shake into another order

explanation.surface: Climb the step, then, unsteady as you are.
explanation.definitionFit: To step up a pace is to speed it, to hurry or accelerate.

clue.text: Understands gun in possession of woman

parts.note: gat is slang for a gun
hers is the pronoun for what belongs to a woman

explanation.surface: Someone works out that a woman is carrying a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: To take it that something is so is to infer or understand.

clue.text: Standing supporter safe, as electric fences off

indicators.note: fencing off encloses, so the answer lies within these words

explanation.surface: An electric fence keeps you safe, as a support stand would.
explanation.definitionFit: A frame on legs that holds an artist's canvas upright.

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as in a pen, so the female deer hold the scrambled word

parts.note: does are female deer

indicators.note: funny means odd, so the letters come out strange

explanation.surface: Women writing comic old drawings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'funny' rearranges OLD into ODL, which 'penning' places inside DOES.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle scribbles or rough drawings made absently.

clue.text: One in ten, say, like vermouth

parts.note: dig is slang for like, as in I dig it
it is Italian vermouth, as in gin and it

explanation.surface: One drink out of ten is like vermouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Fingers are counted on two hands of five; each is one of ten such.

indicators.note: tipping says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Keeping your balance while tipping a table in a pub game.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft left 'in' as a link word; it is the hiding signal. 'in' finds ARBIL across the two words and 'tipping' reverses it. Bar billiards is a British pub table game.
explanation.definitionFit: The zodiac sign is pictured as a pair of scales, a weighing balance.

definitions.meaning: what a police officer does: taking criminals into custody

explanation.surface: A policeman's job is impressive.
explanation.definitionFit: Apprehending suspects is police work; striking or eye-catching is the adjective sense.

clue.text: Black book offered at knock-down price, it's inferred?

indicators.note: a book offered at a cut price is placed within the selling event

parts.note: a sale is an event where goods go at reduced prices

explanation.surface: A black book is being sold cheaply, or so one gathers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's inferred?' admits that the containment is implied rather than stated.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry and poetry the word names the colour black.

parts.note: to add is to put on, as extra
led means ushered or guided

explanation.surface: Someone was put on stage, then shown off it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' looks like part of 'ushered off'; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggs gone bad are rotten, the old sense of this word, so they are spoilt.

indicators.note: defining means setting the bounds of, so the word for very surrounds the work

parts.note: that means very, as in not that big
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: An old picture that is the very definition of a work.
explanation.walkthrough: Top Hat is a 1935 Fred Astaire film.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1935 musical film is an old motion picture.
